keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «과학자들은 우주 물질의 대부분이 보이지 않는다고 생각한다(주제)» 와 «암흑 물질의 수수께끼는 우리가 많이 알아도 우주의 상당 부분이 아직 미지라는 것을 보여 준다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the topic (most of the matter in the universe is invisible) and the conclusion (the mystery of dark matter shows that, despite all our knowledge, much of the universe is still unknown). The green sentences are the answers.

qs.q: Why do scientists call it 'dark' matter?
opts: Because it is found only at night
Because it does not give off, absorb, or reflect light
Because it is made of black rocks
evs: Everything we can see in the universe, from planets to stars to entire galaxies, makes up only a small part of it.
They call it dark matter because it does not give off, absorb, or reflect light.
Yet the biggest surprise is that no one knows what it actually is.
Huge detectors have been built deep underground to catch these particles, but none has been detected so far.
why: 암흑 물질은 빛을 내지도, 흡수하지도, 반사하지도 않아서 «암흑» 이라는 이름이 붙었어요.
It does not give off, absorb, or reflect light, so it is called dark matter.

qs.q: In the text, what does 'should have flown apart' mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 'should have flown apart' 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: should have moved closer to Earth
should have turned into new stars
should have broken up and scattered
evs: Something unseen must be adding extra gravity to hold them together.
Scientists believe that most of the matter in the universe is invisible.
Today, scientists estimate that dark matter makes up about 85 percent of all the matter in the universe.
A small group of researchers even suggests that our understanding of gravity itself may need to change.
why: 바로 다음 문장에서 보이지 않는 무언가가 은하를 «붙잡아 두고(hold them together)» 있다고 했어요. 그러니 flown apart 는 그 반대, 뿔뿔이 흩어져 버린다는 뜻이에요.
The next sentence says something unseen holds the galaxies together. So 'flown apart' means the opposite: breaking up and scattering.

qs.q: How do scientists know dark matter exists even though no one can see it?
qs.qko: 아무도 볼 수 없는데, 과학자들은 암흑 물질이 있다는 것을 어떻게 알까요?
opts: Its gravity speeds up stars at galaxy edges and bends passing light
Underground detectors have caught many dark matter particles
Powerful telescopes can see it reflecting light
evs: She found that stars near the outer edges were moving much faster than expected.
Many scientists think it is made of tiny particles that have not been discovered yet.
Other observations support this idea, such as the way large clusters of galaxies bend the light that passes near them, an effect called gravitational lensing.
They call it dark matter because it does not give off, absorb, or reflect light.
why: 은하 바깥쪽 별들이 예상보다 훨씬 빨리 돌고, 거대한 은하단은 근처를 지나는 빛을 휘게 해요. 두 관측 모두 보이지 않는 물질의 중력을 보여 줘요.
Stars at the outer edges move much faster than expected, and galaxy clusters bend passing light. Both show the gravity of unseen matter.

ends: How do underground detectors try to catch dark matter?
지하 검출기는 암흑 물질을 어떻게 잡으려 할까?
What is dark energy, and how is it different from dark matter?
암흑 에너지는 무엇이고, 암흑 물질과 어떻게 다를까?
